title: Stop The Wedding, Just For A Minute
trend: TikTok 'Stop the Wedding' format ('Stop the wedding, but...' + a petty wedding regret; New Engen TikTok list updated Nov 2 2026, US) — barn wedding where the leaning cake, bride, groom and dog reverend each stop the ceremony over small regrets

intro: a park. a dog reverend. a leaning cake.
youtube_title: Stop The Wedding, Just For A Minute | Funny Cartoon
description:
A park wedding keeps getting stopped by a leaning cake, a very tired bride, a groom in the wrong boots and a dog who got ordained on his lunch break.
Nobody objects to the marriage. They object to the napkins.

#cartoon #animation #funny #comedy #wedding
tiktok_caption: nobody objects to the marriage. they object to the napkins. #cartoon #animation #funny #comedy #wedding

lines.text: We are gathered here in this public park, which cost nine thousand dollars, and is free.
If anyone objects to this union, speak now.
Stop the wedding.
Who said that?
Down here. Table two. I am the cake.
June, the cake is talking.
That cake was six hundred dollars, Curtis. It should do something.
Stop the wedding, but just for a minute. I am leaning.
My top layer has been sliding toward the door since the first song.
Noted. Does the cake object to the marriage?
No. I object to this table. It has three good legs.
Fine. Somebody put a napkin under it.
Not those napkins. Stop the wedding.
June?
Stop the wedding, but I should have gone with the ivory napkins.
These are eggshell. I said yes to eggshell because I was tired.
I have eaten both. There is no difference.
You ate a napkin?
I ate several. I am a reverend, but I am also a dog.
How did we end up hiring a dog?
I got ordained online. They never asked about species.
It was one form. I pressed the button with my nose.
Well, since we stopped. Stop the wedding, but I regret these boots.
I rented them. They are a size nine. I am a size eleven.
Why would you rent a nine?
The man looked at me and said, you look like a nine. It felt nice.
Stop the wedding, but the lights. I hung four thousand twinkle lights.
You cannot see a single one. It is two in the afternoon.
Stop the wedding.
You cannot stop it. You are running it.
Stop the wedding, but this suit has no place for a tail.
My tail has been wagging inside one leg for an hour. I can no longer feel it.
Hello. Still leaning. Has anyone looked at my table?
Okay. No more stopping. Nobody regrets anything. Reverend, please.
Do you, Curtis, take June, knowing what you now know about the napkins?
June, we have to tell them.
Curtis, no. Not in front of the eggshell.
Everybody? Nobody can stop this wedding, and I will tell you why.
We got married in March. At the courthouse. For the dental plan.
Then what did I press with my nose?
Your mother put down the deposit in January, Curtis. It was not refundable.
So we are getting married again, to not waste the money for getting married.
So I have been leaning for nothing?
You are not for nothing. You are for after.
After what?
After the toast. We cut you.
You cut me?
With a big knife. Together. It is very romantic.
And whatever hits the floor is mine. I have waited since Thursday.
Since Thursday. Reverend, why is there a dent in my back left side?
I licked it. Only a little. Every hour.
It was never the table. I am leaning because of you!
Reverend, please. Just finish, so I can sit down and hate these napkins.
By the power vested in me by one form and my nose, you are still married.
You may now take off the boots.
Come here, you nine.
Stop the wedding.
What now?
He has a fork.
Let us pray.
